nbzinbHossen 0.1.0

    • Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM

nbzinbHossen

nbzinbHossen fits

  • negative binomial (NB2) regression with nbreg() (an alternative to MASS::glm.nb()), using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients alternated with Newton–Raphson on log(θ); and
  • zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression with zinbreg() (an alternative to pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin")), using an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits (a fractional-response logistic regression for the zero part and a weighted NB regression for the count part).

No general-purpose optimizer (optim(), nlm(), …) and no glm()/lm() fitting code is used. ZINB standard errors come from an analytic Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood.

Website (function reference + project report): https://armanhossen-am.github.io/nbzinbHossen/

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("armanhossen-am/nbzinbHossen")

Usage 

library(nbzinbHossen)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(nb)
nb$theta                     # 2.264, same as MASS::glm.nb()

# Zero-inflated NB: count covariates | zero-inflation covariates
zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                data = bioChemists)
summary(zinb)
AIC(nb, zinb)

# Predictions: marginal mean, NB mean, and structural-zero probability
nd <- data.frame(fem = "Women", mar = "Married", kid5 = 1, phd = 3, ment = 10)
predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "response")
predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "count")
predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "zero")

Both fitting functions return S3 objects with print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik (so AIC()/BIC() work), fitted, residuals, nobs and predict methods. Use nbreg_control() / zinbreg_control() to change tolerances, iteration limits, or to print the iteration history (trace = TRUE).

Agreement with the reference implementations

On pscl::bioChemists and AER::NMES1988 the maximum absolute differences are about 1e-7 from MASS::glm.nb() for NB, and below 3e-5 from pscl::zeroinfl() for ZINB. The tolerances required by the project are 1e-5 and 1e-3. The full tables are in inst/benchmark/ and in the report.

R CMD check

devtools::check() gives 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes.
